answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities to cryptographic stake burning via a verifiable proof of burn. When identity minting scales with superlinear cost, the required stake burn grows as an exponential function O(2^k) for k identities, imposing prohibitive economic friction. Staking pools lock hard assets like ferrous metal commodity tokens. If an adversarial swarm attempts mass registration, a validator running a deterministic sonnet cadence audits telemetry, while a comet tail checkpoint protocol incinerates collateral, bankrupting attackers quadratically.
